message.content:
{
  "needed": true,
  "prompt": "Frontend implementation instructions — scope: all UI and client-side logic that submit, validate, display, and test the field aliasing change. Do not change server code here; assume the following shared API facts (preserve them explicitly in your implementation):

Shared API facts (must be acknowledged and enforced client-side):
- The server treats name as an alias for title in requests. The server will still persist title in the database.
- Responses from list, detail, create, and update endpoints will include both fields: title and name. Their values will be exactly identical when the server is correct.
- For requests:
  - Create requests must include at least one of title or name. After frontend migration you must send name (do NOT send title). If both title and name are present in the same request the server returns HTTP 422.
  - Update requests may omit both fields. If a request explicitly sets either field to null the server returns HTTP 422.
  - When exactly one of title or name is present, the server applies the title constraints to that value.
- Validation constraint on the value (applies to both request validation client-side and to map expected server errors): non-empty string with length in the inclusive range 1–255. Do NOT automatically trim inputs on the frontend; length must be computed from the raw input including leading/trailing whitespace.

Frontend responsibilities (concrete steps):
1) Data model / DTO mapping
   - Stop using title for user-facing input and display. Use name everywhere in the UI.
   - When receiving API responses, read response.name for display and for initial form values. You may fall back to response.title only for defensive recovery in development logging, but production display must use response.name.
   - When sending create or update requests, send only a JSON property name (e.g. { "name": "..." }). Do NOT send title in the request body. Do NOT send both name and title together.
   - Never send name with the JSON value null. If you need to omit the field in an update, omit it entirely from the request body.

2) Forms and inputs
   - Change form fields/labels to use "Name" (include UX hint such as: "Name (alias for title)").
   - Input behaviour and constraints:
     - Enforce client-side validation that the raw input length is >=1 and <=255 characters.
     - Do NOT trim input automatically on blur or before validation/submission. All length checks count raw characters including whitespace.
     - Do not accept null values; input components should always produce strings. If a user deletes the whole input, mark the field invalid (empty string not allowed).
     - Prevent submission if validation fails (length <1 or >255).
   - Display a live character count that uses the raw string length (including whitespace). Show max 255.
   - Provide explicit help text near the field: "Maps to server title. 1–255 characters. Whitespace counts; we do not trim for you. Do not submit both name and title."

3) Request construction
   - Create: send POST (to existing create endpoint) with body { "name": <raw-string> }.
   - Update: send PATCH/PUT (to existing update endpoint) and include name only if the user actually changed it and the new value is a valid non-empty string. If the user did not change the value, omit name from the request body.
   - Never include title in the request body. Never include name with null.

4) Response handling and display
   - For list and detail views, display response.name.
   - For create and update success responses, use response.name for UI updates and navigation.
   - As a development-time assertion, add an automated dev-only check (unit/integration test or runtime dev-assert) that response.title === response.name. If they differ, surface a console warning or test failure so the server contract mismatch is detected quickly.

5) Error handling and mapping
   - Expect HTTP 422 for these server-side violations: both title and name present; explicit nulls; validation length violations. Map server-provided field errors to the name input.
   - When server returns a 422, prefer to display the server's per-field error message mapped to the name field. If server errors reference title instead of name, translate/display them to the name field with guidance: "Server error on title (alias: name)."
   - Provide fallback messages for common violations if server details are missing: e.g. "Invalid name — must be 1–255 characters, and must not be null. Do not send both name and title."

6) UI/UX constraints and prohibitions
   - Do not implement any automatic trimming of the name value anywhere in the client (neither for validation nor before submission).
   - Do not allow the client to send a request payload that contains both name and title keys.
   - Do not allow explicit null submission for name. If the app needs to support removing the value, coordinate with backend — until backend contract changes, the frontend must not send null.

7) Backwards/edge-case defensive behavior
   - If you receive a response that does not include name but does include title (server regression), temporarily fall back to showing title but log a warning and treat that as a server-contract mismatch.
   - If you receive name and title but they differ, surface a dev-mode error/warning and prefer response.name for display only after warning. Do not attempt to reconcile or submit corrected values back automatically.

8) Tests to add/update
   - Unit tests for client-side validator: raw-length counting, reject empty string, reject >255, accept strings with whitespace.
   - Unit tests to confirm no trimming occurs (e.g., input " abc " length 5 accepted if within bounds).
   - Integration tests that stub/match API behavior covering these flows:
     - Create success: client sends { name } only; server returns { title, name } identical; UI shows name.
     - Create failure: client sends both title and name (simulate or ensure client does not do so) — expect server 422; assert client displays appropriate error.
     - Create failure: server returns 422 for null or too-long or empty — client maps error to name field.
     - Update success: client omits name if unchanged; client includes name when changed.
     - Update failure: client attempts to send name=null — server 422; client displays error.
     - List/detail rendering: UI reads response.name and displays it; record assertion that response.title === response.name in dev tests.
   - End-to-end test: full create -> list -> detail -> update with name flows verifying only name sent in network requests and UI shows name.

9) Developer documentation and migration notes
   - Update local frontend API docs and service-client wrappers to indicate that create/update requests must use the name property (and never title), and that responses include both title and name.
   - Update component docs, form field descriptions, and any public screenshots or help text to refer to "Name (alias for title)".
   - Communicate explicitly with backend: frontend will stop sending title and will only send name. Also tell backend: frontend will assert response.title === response.name in tests.

10) Implementation checklist (concrete code tasks)
   - [ ] Replace label and input name attribute from title -> name in create/update forms and schema definitions.
   - [ ] Implement client-side validator: 1 <= rawString.length <= 255; no trimming.
   - [ ] Ensure submission code builds request bodies that include name only (omit title), and omit name entirely in update if unchanged.
   - [ ] Add request-time guard that prevents building a request containing both title and name keys.
   - [ ] Update response parsing code to use response.name for UI and initial form values.
   - [ ] Add dev-only check that response.title === response.name and make tests fail or log if not.
   - [ ] Update error mapping to attach server 422 messages to the name field and show fallback messages for null/both-provided/length errors.
   - [ ] Add unit/integration/e2e tests described above.

Notes / constraints to strictly obey
- Do not change or assume server endpoints or response shapes beyond the stated shared API facts. Do not invent new API fields or behaviors.
- Do not auto-trim input. All validations must be applied to the raw string value exactly as entered by the user.
- Do not send title in requests at all after this migration. Sending both name+title will trigger server 422.
- Do not send null values for name; an explicit null will produce server 422.

Deliverables
- Updated form components and services that send name in requests and display name in list/detail.
- Validator utilities and tests updated for raw-length validation and no trimming.
- Integration and e2e tests covering the required scenarios.
- Updated frontend docs and a short note to backend owners that frontend assert response.title === response.name in dev/tests.

If any server behavior or endpoint URL is unclear, stop and request clarification from the backend team instead of guessing. The frontend must implement exactly the request/response contract and constraints described above."
}
message.reasoning:
**Clarifying submission requirements**

The requirement states that for front-end migration, I need to submit and display the name rather than the title. I have to ensure that I don't send both name and title at the same time, as that would result in a 422 error. When updating, I can omit both fields for no update, but sending null will also cause a 422. For creating, I must submit a non-null and non-empty name that is between 1 and 255 characters, without trimming. So even whitespace-only is valid, but I must confirm that the length is correctly validated.**Defining form behavior requirements**

When displaying forms, I should prefill the 'name' field using response.name. If responses include both name and title with the same value, I’ll stick with using name. I also need to ensure that the listing and detail views reference response.name for display and local copies. For the input name attribute, I have to use the name field. When sending updates, I should only include the name property if the user has changed it, but I can omit it for an unchanged value. It's crucial to handle errors correctly; if the server returns a 422, I’ll need to check for specific error messages, like both fields being provided or a null value.**Clarifying error handling and validation**

I can't make assumptions about the error structure, so I need to instruct developers to display constraint messages based on HTTP 422 and any error details from the backend. For fallback messages, if both fields are provided, I should indicate, "Do not provide both name and title; send only name" and provide guidance about length and null values. For client-side validation, I need to ensure the input string length is between 1 and 255, without trimming, while also disallowing null values and the title. I’ll need to disable submission if invalid inputs are present. For forms that accept bulk or JSON, the title property shouldn't be included. Additionally, I must create test cases to verify that responses have both fields set to identical values and ensure the frontend checks for equality. It'll be essential to maintain the requirement of preserving constraints for unchanged shared API facts, without omitting any facts just because they're handled on the other side.**Establishing response requirements**

We need to clarify that responses will include both fields as identical values, and the frontend should check for this equality during development tests, logging or warning about any mismatches, which might indicate a server bug. I also have to consider older clients that may not provide a name. The backend could respond with both fields, but I can't make assumptions about older servers. Therefore, I must adhere strictly to the provided facts and only return JSON that matches the specified schema. "prompt" should contain the implementation instructions as a string, and "needed" should be set to true, indicating that frontend changes are necessary. I need to ensure that the prompt content clearly addresses every requirement while preserving unchanged shared API facts. I'm also tasked with providing specific lines and examples of request JSON shapes, such as sending { "name": "..." } for create and update requests, without including the title.**Outlining update and validation requirements**

For updates, I’ll need to use PATCH/PUT as per the current API, explicitly instructing not to include null names or titles. For listing and detail responses, both fields should have identical values, using the name for display. When creating, both fields will be present, again using the name. Forms will label the 'Name' field as "alias for title," guiding users to provide 1-255 characters without automatic trimming, ensuring whitespace counts. I'll need to show raw input length, and any submission should not allow null values. If users want to clear a field, they shouldn't send null, but I might advise sending an empty string. However, an empty string is invalid, so UI must prevent this. A thorough testing strategy will include unit tests for validators, integration tests, and end-to-end tests covering various scenarios, including validations for length and presence of fields. I'll also update all relevant documentation and ensure frontend instructions remain focused without pulling from backend outputs. Now, I’ll draft the prompt string to encapsulate these details and return it as a JSON object, detailing steps in bullet format while avoiding excessive verbosity.
